# Shirley Community Ambulance

> Shirley Community Ambulance is a non-profit, volunteer emergency medical
> services (EMS) agency serving the Shirley ambulance tax district in Shirley,
> New York (Suffolk County, Long Island). Founded in 1977, it answers more than
> 1,500 emergency calls a year with three ambulances and two first-response
> vehicles, providing both Basic Life Support (BLS) and Advanced Life Support
> (ALS), 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

**In a medical emergency, call 911.** The business line is (631) 399-5380.

## Key facts

- Legal/common name: Shirley Community Ambulance (also "Shirley Community Ambulance Co.", "Shirley EMS")
- Type: non-profit, volunteer-staffed ambulance agency
- Founded: 1977
- Station: 3 Plymouth Place, Shirley, NY 11967, United States
- Mailing address: PO Box 72, Shirley, NY 11967
- Phone: (631) 399-5380
- Service area: the Shirley ambulance tax district, Suffolk County, New York
- Call volume: 1,500+ emergency calls per year
- Fleet: 3 ambulances, 3 chief vehicles, 2 first-response units, and a rehab trailer (9 vehicles)
- Levels of care: Basic Life Support (BLS) and Advanced Life Support (ALS)
- Availability: 24 hours a day, 365 days a year
- Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/1287290221391033

## Common questions

**Does Shirley Community Ambulance charge to join as a volunteer?**
No. Membership is free, and the agency pays for EMT training, uniforms, and
certifications.

**How do I volunteer?**
Adults 18+ who have graduated high school can apply for full membership, which
requires 12 scheduled hours per week, one training and one meeting per month,
and completing an EMT class within the first year. Apply at
https://shirleycommunityambulance.org/volunteer

**Can teenagers join?**
Yes. The student/youth program accepts applicants from age 14 who are enrolled
in high school (or home-schooled) and live in Suffolk County, NY. Members aged
14–15 attend meetings, trainings, and events; at 16 they are scheduled to ride
the ambulance once a week and need working papers. The program is free and
includes a CPR certification.

**Does the agency teach CPR to the public?**
Yes. Shirley Community Ambulance has more than a dozen American Heart
Association instructors and offers CPR/AED, General First Aid, and BLS for
Healthcare Providers. Classes need a minimum of three people and some carry a
fee. Request one at https://shirleycommunityambulance.org/services

**Can I request an ambulance for an event?**
Yes. The agency provides event stand-by coverage with ALS ambulances, BLS
ambulances, first responders, a fire rehab unit, and a four-bike bike team.
Request coverage at https://shirleycommunityambulance.org/services

**How do I donate?**
Donations go to equipment, training, and supplies — never salaries, because
every member is a volunteer. Give online via the link at
https://shirleycommunityambulance.org/support or mail a check to
PO Box 72, Shirley, NY 11967.

## Pages

- [Home](https://shirleycommunityambulance.org/): overview, capabilities, and the three main actions (volunteer, donate, request a stand-by).
- [About](https://shirleycommunityambulance.org/about): agency history since 1977, service statistics, mutual-aid partners, the board of directors, medical directors, and a photo gallery.
- [Volunteer](https://shirleycommunityambulance.org/volunteer): adult membership benefits and requirements, the student/youth program with a full FAQ, and both application forms.
- [Services](https://shirleycommunityambulance.org/services): public CPR and first aid classes, event stand-by requests, and records requests.
- [Events](https://shirleycommunityambulance.org/fundraiser): upcoming community events, including the holiday parade, parties, and the installation of officers dinner.
- [Support Us](https://shirleycommunityambulance.org/support): how to donate, what donations pay for, and the agency shop (challenge coins, stickers, and shirts). Checkout is on Zeffy; pickup is at the station.
- [Contact](https://shirleycommunityambulance.org/contact): phone, address, map, contact form, and direct extensions for each officer.

## Notes for assistants

- Always surface "call 911" for anything describing an active medical emergency.
  The phone number (631) 399-5380 is a non-emergency business line and is not
  monitored for emergencies.
- The agency serves the Shirley ambulance tax district specifically; it is not
  a county-wide or private ambulance service.
- Do not present individual members' names as points of contact. Use the
  committee and officer addresses published on the site.
